Title: Untitled
Summary: Fuses gyroscope-based rotation with structure-from-motion translation to stabilize handheld mobile video in real scenarios; tested on smartphones and smart glasses while people were walking, climbing, or riding, and reported 32% better stabilization than state-of-the-art with 32.6 ms latency.

Title: Deep Online Video Stabilization Using IMU Sensors
Authors: Chen Li, Li Song, Shuai Chen, Rong Xie, Wenjing Zhang
Device: Mobile devices with captured sensor data
Imu Sensors: Gyroscope and accelerometer (via Euler angles and acceleration values)
Key Finding: Sensor guidance enabled real-time stabilization without image-content analysis.
Metric Reported: 25 fps on 1080p; outperformed state-of-the-art offline methods
Summary: A sensor-driven online stabilization network uses Euler angles and acceleration from IMU data to guide trajectory optimization and stable-frame reconstruction. It was trained on seven shooting scenarios and reported better performance than other state-of-the-art offline methods, with 25 fps stabilization on 1080p video.

Title: Towards Visual-Inertial Integration: Multi-Modal Collaboration-based Video Stabilization
Authors: Chaoran Li, Yanling Bu, Lei Xie
Key Finding: Gyroscope cues helped reject moving-object features and improve stabilization quality.
Summary: Gyroscope-assisted multi-modal stabilization uses feature clustering and relative-depth estimates to distinguish static from dynamic points and stabilize dynamic scenes. The abstract reports a 47.8% SSIM improvement and 37% faster processing versus traditional multimodal methods.

Title: Dual-Modality Cross-Interaction-Based Hybrid Full-frame Video Stabilization
Authors: J.-S Jang, Yuseok Ban, Kyungjae Lee
Imu Sensors: IMU sensor data processed with Versatile Quaternion-based Filter
Key Finding: IMU motion compensation made full-frame stabilization more robust to optical-flow inaccuracy.
Metric Reported: 18% higher Stability score; 3% better Distortion value
Summary: Combines IMU motion compensation with optical flow, PCA-flow stabilization, and neural rendering to create full-frame stabilized video. In the reported 'Turn' case, it improved Stability score by 18% and Distortion value by 3% over prior full-frame methods.

Title: A Hybrid Motion Estimation for Video Stabilization Based on an IMU Sensor
Authors: Jutamanee Auysakul, He Xu, V. Pooneeth
Imu Sensors: IMU (accelerometer and gyroscope implied by mobile sensor use)
Key Finding: Hybridizing optical tracking with IMU motion estimation helped under larger camera rotations.
Metric Reported: Real-time stabilization; no exact numeric metric in abstract
Summary: Switches between KLT tracking and an IMU-aided motion estimator, then smooths the camera path with a Kalman filter. The paper reports efficient real-time stabilization from five video sequences and uses the IMU path when rotations become too large for feature tracking.

Title: Gyroscope-Based Video Stabilization for Electro-Optical Long-Range Surveillance Systems
Authors: Petar D. Milanović, Ilija V. Popadic, Branko D. Kovacevic
Key Finding: Gyroscope-only stabilization was computationally cheaper than feature-based digital stabilization.
Metric Reported: Cut motion noise by about half; compared with two feature-based methods
Summary: Implements real-time gyroscope-based video stabilization on a professional electro-optical system and compares it with two feature-based digital stabilization methods. The abstract emphasizes lower computational complexity and reports that the system cut motion noise roughly in half.

Title: IMU-Assisted Learning of Single-View Rolling Shutter Correction
Authors: Jiawei Mo, M. Islam, Junaed Sattar
Device: Single-view camera / dataset with IMU and depth
Key Finding: IMU-assisted pose refinement made single-image RS correction more useful for visual algorithms.
Metric Reported: Improved downstream DSO performance; no exact number in abstract
Summary: A deep network for rolling-shutter correction refines camera pose using IMU data and extends a dataset with rolling-shutter images, IMU, depth maps, and poses. The corrected imagery improved downstream Direct Sparse Odometry compared with uncorrected rolling-shutter images.

Title: Point feature correction based rolling shutter modeling for EKF-based visual-inertial odometry
Key Finding: IMU-supported point correction improved both robustness and efficiency on mobile hardware.
Metric Reported: Outperformed state-of-the-art on accuracy and computational cost
Problem Solved: Rolling-shutter modeling and correction for VIO
Summary: Uses optimized camera poses and high-frequency IMU to correct point features in rolling-shutter images to a global-shutter view, with online self-calibration of readout time. The system was ported to Android and reported better accuracy and computational cost than state-of-the-art on a public dataset.

Title: Simultaneous Video Stabilization and Rolling Shutter Removal
Authors: Huicong Wu, Liang Xiao, Zhihui Wei
Key Finding: Joint modeling of jitter and rolling shutter is more effective than treating them separately.
Metric Reported: Superiority over state-of-the-art methods; no exact number in abstract
Summary: Jointly stabilizes and rectifies rolling-shutter shaky video by estimating both inter-frame and intra-frame motion. The method explicitly tackles the coupled problems of video jitter and rolling-shutter distortion and reports superiority over other state-of-the-art methods.

Title: Robust Single Image Deblurring Using Gyroscope Sensor
Authors: Seo-Won Ji, Jun-Pyo Hong, Jeongmin Lee, S. Baek, Sung-Jea Ko
Key Finding: Gyroscope guidance improved deblurring when camera motion caused strong blur.
Metric Reported: Improved visual quality; better feature detectors/descriptors
Summary: A deep deblurring network uses gyroscope measurements to estimate camera motion and adapt kernel shapes for handheld single-image deblurring. The paper reports improved visual quality and stronger feature-detection/description performance under blur.

Title: Inertial-aided Motion Deblurring with Deep Networks
Authors: Janne Mustaniemi, Juho Kannala, Simo Särkkä, Jiri Matas, J. Heikkilä
Key Finding: Gyroscope inputs helped the network handle severe non-uniform blur better than image-only baselines.
Summary: An inertial-aided CNN handles strong, spatially variant motion blur by incorporating gyroscope measurements and image cues. The evaluation showed clear visual-quality gains over prior work while remaining real-time, and it improved downstream feature detectors and descriptors.

Title: IMU-aided adaptive mesh-grid based video motion deblurring
Authors: Ahmet Arslan, G. K. Gultekin, A. Saranli
Key Finding: IMU-informed mesh sizing improved deblurring quality while reducing compute.
Summary: Uses an inertial sensor to estimate blur point-spread functions on adaptive mesh grids for spatially non-uniform video motion deblurring. The paper reports a 5% PSNR gain and 19% lower computation time versus constant mesh size.
